sovereign_country.strategic_role: 西欧核心消费市场、高客单价品牌合规与本土清关

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Online Sales of Maternity and Infant Care Commodities

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (Napoleonic Code tradition; unitary national corporate law without sub-state divergence)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: France-People's Republic of China Bilateral Investment Treaty (signed 30 May 1984, entered into force 1985)
France-India Double Taxation Avoidance Agreement (1992, as amended)
France-Hong Kong SAR Double Taxation Agreement (2010)
France-United States Income Tax Convention and related exchange of letters (as amended through 2009)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Articles L.561-1 to L.561-48 and R.561-1 et seq. of the French Monetary and Financial Code (Code monétaire et financier), especially Article L.561-2-2 (obligation to declare beneficial owners); Articles R.561-2-4 and D.561-2-5; Article L.123-13 of the French Commercial Code (Code de commerce); Loi n° 2016-1691 of 1 December 2016 (Loi Sapin 2); Regulation (EU) 2015/847; Directive (EU) 2015/849 as transposed; TRACFIN supervisory and reporting requirements.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized power of attorney (pouvoir) for SAS incorporation formalities
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary in the domicile of each foreign corporate or individual shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille under the 5 October 1961 Convention; consular legalization at the French Consulate if the issuing state is not an Apostille contracting party

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Extrait K-bis or Certificate of Good Standing of each foreign corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent company registry of the place of incorporation of the foreign shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or, in non-Hague Contracting States, consular legalization by the competent French Consulate

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of passport or national identity card of each beneficial owner and proposed legal representative
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public, judicial officer, or consular office in the country of issuance
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille on the notarial certification or consular legalization by France where the issuing state is not an Apostille member

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of no criminal record (extrait de casier judiciaire / police clearance) for each beneficial owner and proposed legal representative
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Criminal records registry or judicial authority of the state of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or French consular legalization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of tax residence (certificat de résidence fiscale) of the controlling shareholder or proposed legal representative
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent national tax authority of the state of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or French consular legalization

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, directors, and authorized signatories against the OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List, the EU Consolidated Sanctions List, the UN Security Council sanctions lists, and the French domestic surveillance notices issued by TRACFIN. Politically Exposed Persons are determined in accordance with the FATF definition and the implementing provisions of Decree n° 2018-284 of 18 April 2018. Enhanced due diligence applies to any foreign PEP, immediate family members, and close associates. Adverse-media and independent judicial checks are required, and all screening evidence must be retained for at least five years.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Guichet Unique de formalités d'entreprises (formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr) and the INPI Registre National des Entreprises (registre-national-entreprises.fr)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The SAS name must be entered in Latin-alphabet characters. French law under Loi n° 94-665 of 4 August 1994 (Loi Toubon) requires that public and consumer-facing commercial communications in France clearly include a French-language understanding; therefore any foreign-language tradename used for maternity and baby products must be accompanied by a French translation or explanatory equivalent in the statutory articles of association. The RNE database will reject a name that is identical, confusingly similar, or misleadingly similar to an existing company name, registered trademark, or natural person designation where it may cause confusion.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: A name rejection is notified in writing by the Greffe with the factual and legal grounds stated. The applicant may file a petition (requête) before the President of the competent Tribunal judiciaire within 30 calendar days of service, attaching the refusal decision, the draft articles of association, and evidence rebutting the identity or confusion ground. The President must rule expeditiously; where the refusal is reversed, the Greffe is ordered to register the name or the incorporation dossier within 15 days of the final order. If the name is refused because of a third-party trademark, the applicant may re-submit a corrected dossier with an alternative name within the same 30-day reservation window without an additional statutory filing fee for name review.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual office (domiciliation commerciale) is permissible for the SAS provided the registered office is physically located in France at an address operated by a licensed domiciliation company, the domiciliation contract satisfies the requirements of Article L.123-11-2 of the French Commercial Code, and the office receives all legal notices and mail. For an online maternity and baby supplies commerce company, no statutory physical point-of-sale is required, but product safety compliance under consumer protection regulations may require records to be kept at a designated address.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low unannounced inspection probability of approximately 5-10% annually at the virtual office address, mainly by the Direction Générale de la Concurrence, de la Consommation et de la Répression des Fraudes (DGCCRF) for consumer-safety and supply-chain checks; the physical warehouse or fulfillment center, if located in France, carries a higher unannounced inspection probability of around 10-15%.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Government filing fee for the registration dossier submitted through the Guichet Unique and the RNE/Greffe
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce / INPI
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff fixed by the French Ministry of Justice annual arrêté

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Compulsory publication of the constitution notice (avis de constitution) in a licensed legal announcements gazette (journal d'annonces légales)
First-year domiciliation fee for a licensed virtual office and registered address
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark EUR 30-80 per month

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarization and apostille/consular legalization of powers of attorney and shareholder identity documentation
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Notary in the country of signature and French Consulate where applicable
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory notarial fee schedule of the origin country plus fixed consular charges

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: UBO piercing, PEP, and domestic and international sanctions screening report
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: French authorized legal or compliance firm
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Fixed compliance fee or blended hourly rate of EUR 200-400

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Preparation and signature/notarization of the SAS articles of association (statuts)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: French avocat or other admitted legal practitioner
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market fixed rate for a standard SAS incorporation, EUR 900-1,300

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Opening of a provisional blocked bank account for cash capital contribution if applicable
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: French bank or Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Sworn translation into French of UBO and corporate documents from a foreign origin language
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Traducteur expert près un tribunal (court-expert translator)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Regulated or market tariff per page

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: France, Code de commerce, Articles L.227-1 to L.227-20 (SAS regime), L.210-1, L.210-6, and R.123-30 et seq. (RCS formalities); implementing decree Décret n°67-236 du 23 mars 1967, as amended.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Guichet Unique des Formalités des Entreprises (operated by INPI) transmitting to the Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), administered by the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce de Paris.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Cerfa n°11678 (Form M0), electronic immatriculation dossier for a legal entity, including the annex PF-0 and the RBE beneficial-ownership schedule, filed via guichet-entreprises.service-public.fr.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum capital for an SAS (Art. L.227-2 alinéa 1 C. com.); cash contributions must be paid up to at least 50% upon incorporation (alinéa 2), with the balance payable within 5 years; in-kind contributions must be fully paid upon subscription; paid-up cash must be blocked in escrow with a French bank, a notary or the Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations until the Kbis registration certificate is delivered.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: By unanimous decision of the shareholders and executive officers of the proposed SAS, made subject to registration, the following is resolved: (1) the draft Articles of Association are adopted exactly as signed; (2) the share subscriptions, capital blocking certificate and the non-cash contribution report are approved; (3) the registered office is fixed at 15 Rue de la Paix, 75002 Paris, France; (4) [NAME] is appointed Président with full authority to represent the Company toward third parties; (5) [NAME] is appointed Directeur Général; (6) signatory authorities and indemnification are established; (7) all formalities for public-notice publication and RCS registration through the Guichet Unique are authorized, with power to attorn to counsel.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Name Verification and Availability Check
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: INPI (Base Sirene) and Infogreffe/INSEE — negative search; no formal name reservation is required for SAS incorporation.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Run a negative search of the proposed corporate name across the RCS, Infogreffe and INPI trademark databases to confirm availability; verify that no conflicting French or EU trademark exists; select a primary name plus two fallback names for inclusion in the Articles; register the matching domain name if commercially desirable.
required_dossiers: List of three proposed corporate names
Negative search results from INPI/Infogreffe
List of founding shareholders and their corporate names
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused or conflicts with a prior trademark, substitute one of the fallback names in the Articles and re-file; no administrative appeal is warranted before substitution.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting, Valuation and Signature of the Articles of Association (Statuts)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Founding shareholders acting unanimously; optional notary (notaire) required when real-property or high-value in-kind contributions are contributed.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the statuts in French setting out the SAS legal form, corporate purpose covering ISIC 4791 online retail of maternity and infant supplies, registered office, share capital and contribution details, 99-year duration, appointment and powers of the Président, share-transfer restrictions, and statutory-auditor conditions; obtain each shareholder's signature; if notarial, execute an authenticated deed and pay notarial fees; attach the commissaire aux apports valuation report for any in-kind contribution.
required_dossiers: Identity documents (national ID or passport) of all shareholders
Notarized power of attorney for non-resident or remote signatories
Bank capital-blocking certificate (attestation de blocage)
Contribution valuation report by a statutory auditor if in-kind contributions exist
Registered-office proof (lease, ownership deed or domiciliation agreement)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry queries the Articles, amend the defective clauses, obtain fresh signatures from all shareholders, and resubmit a revised M0 package with a corrected RBE where applicable.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening of a Capital Deposit Account and Blocking of Funds
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: An authorized credit institution established in France, the Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations, or a notary.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary frozen business account in the name of the company in formation; transfer the subscribed cash capital; obtain the attestation de blocage certifying that funds will be released only against presentation of the RCS registration certificate (extrait Kbis); deliver the certificate to the legal counsel for inclusion in the filing package.
required_dossiers: Final draft of the Articles of Association
Identity documents of the founding shareholders
Signed foundation resolution
Bank KYC/AML questionnaires and source-of-funds declarations
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank delays issuance, instruct the bank in writing with the final Articles and corporate purpose; if still unresolved, transfer the escrow mandate to a notary or the Caisse des Dépôts and obtain a substitute blocking certificate.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication of the Legal Incorporation Announcement (Avis de Constitution)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Journal d'annonces légales (JAL) authorized by the Prefecture of the department where the registered office is located.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Publish a legal notice stating the exact corporate name, legal form (SAS), share capital, registered office address, corporate object, duration, and the identity and powers of the Président and Directeur Général; pay the publication fee; obtain the attestation de parution from the JAL editor.
required_dossiers: Draft legal-notice text
Copy of the signed Articles of Association
Statement of corporate purpose and intended RCS registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the JAL declines or misprints the notice, publish a corrective notice and obtain a fresh attestation; only the corrected publication certificate may be attached to the M0 filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Compilation of the M0 Dossier and Beneficial Ownership (RBE) Declaration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Founding counsel and the future Président — final assembly prior to submission to the Guichet Unique.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the Cerfa n°11678 (M0) form and the RBE schedule identifying each natural person owning more than 25% of capital or voting rights or otherwise exercising control; collect all original annexes, including the signed statuts, JAL attestation, capital-blocking certificate, registered-office lease, officer identity proofs, capacity statements and declarations of non-conviction for legal representatives; verify that all shareholders have signed each page of the Articles.
required_dossiers: Cerfa n°11678 (M0) and PF-0 annex
RBE beneficial-owner declaration
Signed and initialed Articles of Association
JAL publication certificate (attestation de parution)
Capital-blocking certificate
Registered-office lease or domiciliation agreement
Identity and residential address of the Président and Directeur Général
Declarations of non-conviction and acceptance of office for each officer
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: An incomplete RBE blocks the filing and may expose the parties to fines under Article L.561-6 of the Code monétaire et financier; promptly correct the RBE schedule and resubmit; if a beneficial owner cannot be identified, file a reasoned statement and legal opinion with the dossier.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic Submission to the Guichet Unique (INPI) and RCS Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Guichet Unique des Formalités des Entreprises (INPI), with downstream verification by the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log onto the Guichet Unique portal, select 'Société par Actions Simplifiée — immatriculation', upload the complete M0 package, pay the official state fee of approximately €37.94, and sign electronically or through a delegated attorney/notary; track the automated receipt; the registry verifies legality of the Articles and the RBE, then registers the company and issues the formation certificate.
required_dossiers: Electronic M0 form completed in full
RBE schedule uploaded in the portal
Scanned certified copy of the signed Articles
All annexes compiled in Step 5
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry issues a rejection, the specific grounds appear in the portal; rectify the defects and resubmit within the stated cure period (standard 15 days); if the registry remains silent beyond 15 working days, the founder may petition the President of the Commercial Court for an order compelling registration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Issuance of Kbis Extract, SIREN/SIRET Codes and Post-Registration Filings
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce de Paris (RCS) — issue of the extr… and company identifiers.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon approval, obtain the official extrait Kbis, the only conclusive proof of legal existence, together with SIREN, SIRET and APE codes; present the Kbis to the bank to lift the capital blockage; complete mandatory post-registration steps: URSSAF registration for social contributions, affiliation with an occupational health service, subscription to professional civil-liability insurance, activation of the Stripe and PayPal payment rails with Kbis evidence, and entry of the company into any applicable economic register.
required_dossiers: Approved registration confirmation from the Guichet Unique
Extrait Kbis
SIREN/SIRET/APE attribution slip
Bank release order for blocked capital (levée de blocage)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank or registry delays the Kbis or the release of funds, serve a formal notice upon the Greffe under Article R.123-91 C. com.; if the Kbis is not issued within statutory deadlines, seek an expedited order from the President of the Commercial Court to compel delivery.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: No sector-specific operating license is required for ISIC 4791 (online retail of maternity and infant supplies). Oversight is exercised by the DGCCRF for consumer-product safety under Regulation (EU) 2023/988 and by the DREAL and the Préfecture for any warehouse facility subject to the ICPE environmental regime.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Exempt from statutory license for the core e-commerce activity; an ICPE declaration or registration authorization (Rubrique 1510 — Entrepôts couverts) is required only if a covered logistics warehouse exceeding 500 m³ of storage volume is operated.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministère de la Transition écologique et de la Cohésion des territoires — DREAL (Direction régionale de l'environnement, de l'aménagement et du logement) of the Ile-de-France region.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: ICPE Rubrique 1510: simple déclaration for 500 m³ ≤ V < 20,000 m³; enregistrement for 20,000 m³ ≤ V < 50,000 m³; full environmental authorization (EIA) for V ≥ 50,000 m³. A pure e-commerce warehouse without storage capacity exceeding the threshold is exempt from prior environmental approval.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Arrêté ministériel du 11 avril 2017 (ICPE-déclaration/1510): wastewater discharged to municipal sewer must meet BOD5 ≤ 100 mg/L, COD ≤ 300 mg/L, TSS ≤ 100 mg/L and pH 5.5–9.5; storm-water retention and treatment required; packaging waste must be managed under the AGEC extended-producer-responsibility regime with packaging declared in the SIM/CIEL registry; a waste traceability log must evidence final recovery or recycling of all discarded packaging streams.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety: compliance with Code du travail Articles R.4227-1 et seq. (fire extinguishers, emergency exits, alarms and evacuation drills) for employee-only logistics or office premises; any customer-accessible showroom or pickup point triggers ERP (type M) classification and inspection by the departmental fire safety commission (commission de sécurité). Occupational clearance: mandatory Document Unique d'Évaluation des Risques Professionnels (DUERP), affiliation with an occupational health service under Article L.4624-1 C. trav., structural and load inspection certificate issued by an approved bureau de contrôle (e.g., SOCOTEC or Apave), and the lessor's conformity certificate for the leased facility.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP) - Service des Impôts des Entreprises (SIE) for direct taxes and VAT; professional portal: impots.gouv.fr and GEST; corporate registration platform: formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr (Guichet unique). Export and customs supervision: Direction Générale des Douanes et Droits Indirects (DGDDI), portal: pro.douane.gouv.fr.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a foreign-owned French SAS: non-resident shareholders appoint a French resident legal representative and registered office; submit the incorporation dossier electronically through the Guichet unique at formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr. Upon completion, the company receives Kbis/SIREN, INSEE generates SIRET and NAF/APE code, and the tax administration issues a French VAT identification number (TVA intracommunautaire) in the format 'FR' + 2-digit key + 9-digit SIREN. If the foreign entity operates without forming a French company but is carrying out taxable transactions in France, it must register directly for VAT at the Centre des Impôts des Non-Résidents (CINR); non-EU businesses may be required to appoint a tax representative under Article 289A CGI where no EU establishment exists.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: French law has no US-style check-the-box election; a SAS is irrevocably a corporate entity taxable at entity level under Article 206(1) CGI. Available elections include: (i) fiscal integration / consolidation under Article 223A CGI when a 95% parent controls the SAS; (ii) VAT grouping election (assujetti unique) under Article 256C CGI for closely connected French entities; (iii) waiver of the small-business VAT exemption (renonciation à la franchise en base) under Article 293B CGI. Hybrid mismatch treatment is non-elective and governed by mandatory EU ATAD implementation (Articles 209, 212 bis B, 209 B bis CGI); no check-the-box hybrid section 988 or branch mismatch election exists.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutée - TVA)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: €85,000 annual turnover exclusive of VAT for sales of goods (Article 293B CGI) as the small-business VAT exemption threshold; €37,500 for services. A French SAS is subject to VAT registration from the first taxable transaction unless it qualifies for and remains within the franchise en base de TVA. The threshold applies to French-established enterprises; foreign distance sellers may be required to register from the first euro unless using the EU OSS/IOSS regimes.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: France has implemented a mandatory structured electronic invoicing/e-reporting reform under Article 289(VI) CGI. B2B invoices must be exchanged in structured electronic form through an accredited dematerialization platform (PDP) or the national Public Portal (Portail Public de Facturation - PPF); B2C transaction data must be transmitted through e-reporting to the DGFiP in near-real-time, using the European EN16931 / Factur-X syntax and standard API interfaces. This is a data-clearance model rather than a pre-approval stamping model: fiscal clearance is performed centrally on transaction data after issuance, without digital stamping. Mandatory phases: 1 September 2026 for large and mid-cap enterprises; 1 September 2027 for SMEs and micro-enterprises; non-compliance is sanctionable by graduated administrative fines.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Sales of goods physically dispatched or transported by or on behalf of the supplier to a destination outside the European Union qualify for VAT zero-rating under Article 262(I) CGI. The supplier must retain documentary proof that the goods left the EU customs territory before claiming 0% VAT; title and risk must pass to the non-EU customer. Intra-EU B2B supplies are exempt under Article 262 ter CGI only where the customer provides a valid EU VAT identification number and acquisition VAT is accounted for. For cross-border B2B services connected to export supplies, the place of supply rules under Article 259-1 CGI may render the service outside French VAT where the recipient is outside France.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Déclaration d'exportation / DEX submitted via DGDDI DELTA system) with MRN (Movement Reference Number)
International transport document: Bill of Lading, CMR, CIM or Air Waybill evidencing departure from EU territory
Inward Remittance Certificate / bank payment confirmation evidencing the foreign buyer's settlement of the export invoice
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The DGFiP and DGDDI scrutinize export substantiation files; any missing, contradictory or unverifiable customs or transport documentation will trigger immediate re-taxation of the sale at standard French VAT (20%) plus late-payment interest and penalties. Intentional misclassification or fabrication of export documents attracts the Article 1729 CGI 80% penalty for bad-faith concealment, or up to 100% in cases of abuse of law under Article 1729-0 CGI. Fraudulent export zero-rating may also give rise to criminal tax fraud prosecution under Article 1741 CGI with significant fines and imprisonment. Late or non-repatriation of export proceeds beyond the 180-day financial benchmark may invalidate the invoice-payment evidence required in a VAT refund/export audit, and can expose the exporter to a denial of the zero-rating benefit and recovery of input VAT previously deducted.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France (Bank of France) within the Eurosystem, with foreign-exchange and balance-of-payments statistics administered by the Banque de France and the Direction Generale du Tresor; prudential banking supervision and AML/CFT controls are enforced by the ACPR (Autorite de Controle Prudentiel et de Resolution).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Full convertibility: France has no exchange controls since 1990 and applies the TFEU Articles 63-65 free-movement-of-capital regime; the euro is freely convertible on current and capital account. No prior administrative clearance is required for equity injection, trade settlement, or profit repatriation for a non-sensitive e-commerce business (ISIC 4791). The residual constraints are fiscal and statistical: outbound dividends may attract treaty-based or domestic withholding tax; every cross-border payment above EUR 10,000 is captured in the bank's FICOBA reporting to the French state; direct investment operations of EUR 15,000,000 or more per transaction require a Banque de France balance-of-payments declaration.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. France imposes no statutory surrender, repatriation deadline, or mandatory conversion ratio on export proceeds; receipts may be retained in any currency in any bank, in France or abroad. The only obligations are informational: cross-border transactions exceeding EUR 10,000 are reported by the bank through FICOBA, and direct-investment flows above EUR 15,000,000 per operation are declared to the Banque de France for balance-of-payments statistics.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account (Compte de Depot de Capital) plus Operational Current Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: HIGH for EU/EEA-licensed EMIs passported into France under PSD2 (e.g., Qonto, licensed by the ACPR; Wise Europe, Belgian passport) because they permit fully remote onboarding, euro and multi-currency IBANs, and direct card/PayPal/Stripe settlement. Rating: LOW-MEDIUM for offshore digital EMIs without an EU passport: they are not ACPR-supervised, cannot provide a French euro IBAN, and fail the bank-reference expectation of Tier-1 French banks; they are acceptable only as auxiliary collection/wallet gateways and never as the sole operating account of the French SAS.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: No absolute statutory face-to-face mandate exists: Article L.561-5 of the French Monetary and Financial Code and Decree 2018-284 permit identity verification through qualified remote or eIDAS means. In practice, Tier-1 banks require at least one physical KYC interview (or an equivalent videoconference with full sworn translations and apostille) for non-resident directors and UBOs; fully remote onboarding is reliably available only with ACPR-regulated digital EMIs. For the non-resident-owned SAS, the recommended path is one in-person session at the Paris branch, supported by the source-of-funds and bank-reference dossier.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident director or UBO located outside the EEA, especially in a FATF-grey-listed or high-risk third country, without an existing French banking relationship.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Apostilled and sworn-translated passports; recent proof of address; a formal bank-reference letter (attestation de bancarisation) from the originating bank; 6-12 months of clean bank statements; a source-of-funds file for the capital contribution (boards resolutions, shareholder loan agreement, salary/tax records); and the completed French UBO declaration.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Newly incorporated SAS without French credit history, audited financials or demonstrated commercial substance at onboarding.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: RCS/Kbis extract, notarised statuts, proof of registered office or domiciliation agreement; a credible 3-year business plan; parent-entity financial statements and board resolution; marketplace substance evidence (Stripe/PayPal merchant IDs and processing screenshots); and the French VAT registration number.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: E-commerce flows flagged as card-not-present risk, with high platform concentration or abnormal refund/dispute ratios.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: 12-month processing statements from Stripe/PayPal; monthly turnover and dispute metrics; VAT returns (CA3 or E-TVA) and customs import records for the baby-products category; returns/refund policy; supplier contracts showing Incoterms and order flows.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Third-country supplier payments (mainly China/Hong Kong) triggering sanctions screening or opaque beneficial-ownership review.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Commercial invoices and supply contracts with Incoterms; the supplier's business licence and export credentials; customs/import documentation (entry summary declarations) proving physical trade; a full beneficial-ownership declaration of the supplier; confirmation that no sanctioned party appears on any watchlist.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: For the initial SAS capital, funds are placed in a blocked capital-escrow account (compte de depot de capital) held with a French notary, a Tier-1 French bank, or the Caisse des Depots et Consignations; the depositary issues the attestation de depot des fonds and releases the balance to the operating account after RCS/Kbis registration. Route: SEPA Credit Transfer for EU shareholders; SWIFT MT103 for non-EU parents, with ISO 20022 purpose code 'EQUI' (equity financing) and intra-group code 'INTC' in the Remittance Information field. No exchange-control authorisation is needed; the compliance pack comprises the capital-deposit certificate, statuts, UBO forms, parent board resolutions, and proof of the legal origin of the funds.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Clearing rails: SEPA Credit Transfer for intra-EU EUR disbursements; SWIFT MT103 for open-account payments in EUR/USD/CNH to international suppliers; commercial letters of credit under UCP 600 (MT700 issuance, MT103/MT202 settlement) for initial import batches; documentary collections (D/P, D/A) as a moderate-cost alternative; and DELTA-G/E-DOUANE for French customs VAT/duty. Recommended supplier structure: confirmed sight L/C for the first one or two batches of maternity/baby goods, migrating to open-account MT103 at 30-60 days after a clean delivery and compliance track record.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright FX forward (change a terme) on EUR/USD and EUR/CNH
FX swaps (swap de change) for tenor alignment and interbank settlement
Cross-currency interest-rate swaps (CCIRS) for medium-term financing hedges
European FX options and option collars
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on onshore CNY for the CNH-non-hedgeable portion
Exchange-traded currency futures on EUR/USD as an EMIR-compliant alternative

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Reduced rate of 15% on first EUR 42,500 of taxable profit for enterprises with annual turnover below EUR 10 million; 25% standard rate above threshold; no general statutory tax holiday for SAS e-commerce entities; certain research tax credit (CIR) and innovation tax credit may reduce effective burden.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 2065 (liassex fiscale) plus SIELE electronic filing; mandatory EFI (Echanges de Fichiers Informatisés) via impots.gouv.fr professional transmission
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Filed by the second business day following May 3 of the year following the fiscal year-end; for fiscal years ending December 31, deadline is generally May 3 (or next business day) unless extended; must be filed within 60 days following the close of the fiscal year when the fiscal year does not coincide with the calendar year (under certain conditions).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Identification of the entity: SIREN, SIRET, corporate form (SAS), registered address, tax administration reference code
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident corporate owners must provide their country of residence and any permanent establishment details; clear declaration of French fiscal representative is required if no PE in France.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross profit or operating income reported from French-sourced commercial e-commerce activities
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: All income from cross-border online sales to French consumers must be reported if sourced through a French permanent establishment; otherwise report French-source royalties or services under specific withholding rules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Operating expenses, depreciation, and provisions attributable to French operations
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Expenses must be supported by invoices, transfer pricing documentation, and arm's length substantiation; no arbitrary deduction of head-office charges without economic substance.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax result arising from ordinary operations and exceptional items
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident entities must report profit attributable to the French PE at arm's length; a mere SAS registered office without economic substance will not shift the true place of taxation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax loss carried forward utilized in the current year, up to EUR 1,000,000 plus 50% of the excess taxable profit; remainder cap applies
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Losses of a French SAS may be carried forward five years; non-resident entities without PE cannot carry forward French-source losses.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reduced 15% rate on first EUR 42,500 of taxable profit (when annual turnover below EUR 10 million); balance taxed at 25%
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The reduced band applies only to French-resident entities; non-resident PE taxable profit is assessed at the standard 25% rate unless treaty or domestic provision grants otherwise.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Corporate income tax computed before credits, plus contributions: social solidarity contribution (contribution sociale sur les bénéfices) of 3.3% on retained taxable profit exceeding EUR 763,000 for companies with turnover above EUR 20 million
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Social solidarity contribution applies to French-resident entities with turnover thresholds; non-resident PE is subject to the same contribution when turnover attributable to the French PE exceeds the threshold.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax credits, including CIR (research credit), CICE (historically, now discontinued), or withholding tax credits
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident entities may claim treaty tax credits only through the French PE filing; direct claims from outside France are not accepted on Form 2065.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Final tax due after offset of instalments (imputations) and declaration of balances
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Quarterly instalments are required under the normal regime; a small-business exemption may apply when annual tax is below EUR 3,000; non-resident PE filers must pay through a French bank account or accredited intermediary.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty: 5% of tax due, increased to 10% if not filed within 30 days of formal notice, plus monthly interest of 0.20% per month on unpaid tax; also EUR 60 minimum penalty for each omitted return or document. Additional surcharges of 0.10% per month apply for late payment after the deadlines. Directors could be personally assessed for deliberate obstruction of tax collection under joint and several liability rules.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 30% (25% domestic rate plus 12.8% dividend-withholding levy, subject to exemptions and treaty reduction); standard dividend withholding tax at 30% for non-residents, with a 10% administrative surcharge in certain non-cooperative cases.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke double tax treaty relief (e.g., France-HKSAR DTA at 10% dividend withholding or other applicable DTA), the non-resident shareholder must deliver a valid Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) issued by its jurisdiction of residence, complete French Form 5001/5002 (or EU Directive relief forms, Form 5002 for simplified procedure), and present these to the French paying agent before distribution; refund claims are filed via Form 5003 within the statutory deadlines. The French tax administration applies beneficial ownership tests and economic substance checks.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory royalty withholding 33.33% in the absence of treaty, reduced to 0% under France-HKSAR DTA for fully-assessed intellectual property royalties; interest withholding generally 0% for non-resident creditors under domestic rules, but treaty rate 10% or 0% may apply under the specific DTA; all exemptions require TRC and beneficial ownership declaration.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EUR 400 million consolidated group revenue (where the group includes the French entity and meets CbCR threshold); Local File must be maintained when the French entity's related-party transactions exceed EUR 400 million group revenue, or when the French entity's own annual related-party turnover exceeds EUR 50 million (Article L.13AA of the French Tax Procedures Code); Master File and Local File thresholds are aligned to CbCR and EU requirements; a simplified documentation obligation applies to intermediate entities with turnover below EUR 50 million.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: France follows the OECD Transfer Pricing Guidelines and general anti-abuse provisions (abus de droit) under L.64 of the Tax Procedures Code; although not adopting the EU ESR Artificiality Test, the French doctrine requires sufficient economic substance (employees, offices, management decisions, and operational control in France) for an SAS to be recognized as a taxable resident; treaty benefits are denied where a shell parent in a zero-tax jurisdiction lacks substance and the French SAS is controlled from abroad (test of de facto management, Art. 209 B IE and SAAR rules).

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Undervaluation of cross-border sales, failure to declare French-source revenue, fictitious invoicing, or artificially shifting profit to a zero-tax jurisdiction without operational substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: 40% or 80% moral intentionality penalty on understated tax (Articles 1728 and 1729 CGI), plus 100% penalty for concealment, and interest at 0.20% per month; criminal prosecution possible for tax fraud (fraude fiscale) under Article 1741 of the General Tax Code, carrying a penalty of up to EUR 1,000,000 and imprisonment of 5 years (up to EUR 2,000,000 and 7 years for aggravating circumstances).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be criminally liable for tax fraud or complicity; civil joint and several liability for unpaid corporate tax when fraudulent manoeuvre occurred; travel bans are available in the framework of criminal proceedings and banking restrictions; in serious cases, a director can be personally disqualified and subject to asset seizure.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Creating an SAS that lacks real activity in France while controlling e-commerce operations from a low-tax jurisdiction, or using mail-forwarding and virtual offices to claim French tax residence without managerial substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Recharacterization of the SAS as transparent, denial of treaty benefits, application of the French anti-abuse doctrine, imposition of a 100% solidary penalty for abusive transaction, and assessment of hidden income at EUR 0 (reverse burden); potential application of the EU ATAD anti-hybrid rules.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who orchestrate artificial setups are jointly and severally liable for the full tax debt; can face a personal sanction equal to 5% to 10% of the hidden tax base; imprisonment up to 5 years where criminal evasion is established.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to maintain or file the French master file/local file within 30 days of the request; not aligning intercompany pricing for e-commerce margins and logistics costs with arm's length standards; absence of a clear TP policy for the online distribution of baby/maternity supplies
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fixed penalty of EUR 10,000 per file not provided, or EUR 100 per page up to the same cap; each missing document is assessed separately; potential recharacterization of profit and double taxation; 40% penalty on adjusted corporate tax base.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign transfer pricing documentation declarations are personally liable for false documentation; can be criminally prosecuted for false statements of value or wilful misrepresentation; the tax administration may hold the director jointly liable when acting maliciously.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using non-compliant payment channels (unlicensed platforms) to route Stripe/PayPal settlement funds offshore; knowingly accepting proceeds without customer verification, or structuring payments to evade reporting obligations
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: French Monetary and Financial Code penalties up to EUR 375,000 and imprisonment up to 5 years for money laundering; fines up to 5% of turnover for corporations; payment institutions may be blacklisted; temporary or permanent prohibition of commercial activity.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and beneficial owners of the SAS may be personally prosecuted for AML violations under the Criminal Code; assets seized, travel bans issued, and the corporate veil pierced where the SAS is merely an instrumentality of fraud.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Failure to Appoint Statutory Auditor / Accounting Irregularities
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: SAS exceeding two of the three thresholds (turnover > EUR 8 million, balance sheet > EUR 4 million, 50+ employees) failing to appoint a statutory auditor; or maintaining fictitious contracted accounting records for e-commerce inventory and sales
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal fine of EUR 9,000 and imprisonment of 6 months for directors for non-appointment; administrative penalty of EUR 1,500 for failure to file accounts with the registry; nullity of certain corporate decisions possible; additional tax penalties for untruthful tax returns.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are personally liable for the consequences of missing statutory controls; civil liability for losses caused by inaccurate financial statements; criminal consequences for knowingly signing filings containing false information.
